biological.citation: Voltage-gated potassium channels and genetic epilepsy (PMID: 39434833)
biological.summary: KCNQ3 is a voltage-gated potassium channel implicated in genetic epilepsy. Both gain and loss-of-function mutations in KCNQ3 lead to epilepsy with similar phenotypes through different mechanisms, representing a major focus for precise treatment development.

biological.citation: Solving the Etiology of Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy with Spike-Wave Activation in Sleep (PMID: 39096015)
biological.summary: KCNQ3 was identified as a novel D/EE-SWAS gene in patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. Brain-specific gene co-expression analysis showed D/EE-SWAS genes including KCNQ3 are highly co-expressed in brain, highlighting the importance of channelopathies in these disorders.

biological.citation: Lipophilic compounds restore function to neurodevelopmental-associated KCNQ3 mutations (PMID: 39300259)
biological.summary: Using voltage clamp fluorometry and electrophysiology, researchers identified two distinctive mechanisms by which loss- and gain-of-function NDD-associated mutations in KCNQ3 affect channel gating through S4 movement or S4-to-pore coupling. Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) targeting the voltage-sensing domain achieved partial and complete functional restoration in R227Q- and R236C-containing channels, respectively.

biological.citation: Intellectual Disability and Potassium Channelopathies: A Systematic Review (PMID: 32655623)
biological.summary: KCNQ3 is identified as one of 19 potassium channelopathies associated with intellectual disability. The review documents that KCNQ3 presents both gain- and loss-of-function properties in ID cases, though the mechanisms by which both types of mutations lead to ID remain largely unknown.

biological.citation: Neurocardiac pathologies associated with potassium channelopathies (PMID: 39087855)
biological.summary: KCNQ3 encodes Kv7.3, a delayed rectifier potassium channel with expression in both brain and heart. KCNQ3 variants are associated with severe and refractory epilepsy, and Kv7 channel modulators provide potential anti-seizure therapy, particularly for intractable epilepsy.

biological.citation: Molecular and circuit determinants in the globus pallidus mediating control of cocaine-induced behavioral plasticity (PMID: 39153478)
biological.summary: KCNQ3 expression was downregulated in globus pallidus parvalbumin-positive cells following cocaine exposure, contributing to elevation in cell excitability. Acutely activating KCNQ3-containing channels using carnosic acid reduced cell excitability and impaired cocaine reward and intake, indicating therapeutic potential.

biological.citation: KCNQ5 Controls Perivascular Adipose Tissue-Mediated Vasodilation (PMID: 38354270)
biological.summary: KCNQ3 is part of the KV7 family of voltage-gated potassium channels that control smooth muscle cell membrane potential and vascular tone. Genetic mouse models targeting Kcnq3 were used to demonstrate the role of KV7 channels in adipose-vascular coupling and vasodilation.

biological.citation: Constitutive opening of the Kv7.2 pore activation gate causes KCNQ2-developmental encephalopathy (PMID: 39602259)
biological.summary: The paralogous KCNQ3 A356T variant was investigated alongside KCNQ2 variants (A317T, L318V) affecting the S6 activation gate. All-atom molecular dynamics simulations revealed that mutations stabilize a constitutively open channel configuration in the closed state, representing a molecular pathogenetic mechanism for KCNQ-related encephalopathies.

biological.citation: ASHG 2022 - The impact of NGS on rare and complex epilepsies (C. Gellera et al.)
biological.summary: KCNQ3 was identified as a causative gene in patients with severe and complex generalized epilepsies and developmental epileptic encephalopathies. In vitro electrophysiological studies in CHO cells demonstrated pathogenic roles of KCNQ3 variants, and retigabine (a KCNQ2/3 activator) showed significant clinical improvement in patients carrying specific variants.

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - Large-scale targeted sequencing identifies risk genes for autism and developmental delay (T. Wang et al.)
biological.summary: KCNQ3 showed evidence of increased mutational burden in neurodevelopmental disorder cases (autism spectrum disorder and developmental delay) compared to controls in a large-scale targeted sequencing study of 18,836 NDD cases.
biological.sample_size: 18,836 NDD cases (9,710 ASD, 9,126 DD) vs 45,376 controls
